identity.title: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement

problem.claim: Develop LLM-based evaluation that selectively trusts judge-model decisions to align with human judgments at a user-specified agreement level.

contributions.claim: Selective Evaluation assesses judge confidence and escalates uncertain cases instead of relying uncritically on model preferences.
Simulated Annotators is introduced as a confidence-estimation method intended to improve judge calibration and coverage.
Cascaded Selective Evaluation uses cheaper initial judges and escalates only when necessary while retaining the stated human-agreement guarantee.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize Simulated Annotators as a novel confidence-estimation method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Cascaded Selective Evaluation guarantees strong human alignment beyond LLM judging without selective evaluation.

On a Chatbot Arena subset, the authors report that their method, using cost-effective models such as Mistral-7B, guarantees over 80% human agreement with almost 80% test coverage, whereas GPT-4 almost never reaches 80% agreement there.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper argues that pairwise evaluation should estimate judge confidence and selectively trust decisions rather than rely uncritically on model preferences.
It presents Selective Evaluation with a stated provable guarantee of human agreement at a user-specified level.
It introduces Simulated Annotators to improve calibration and enable high evaluation coverage.
It proposes escalating from cheaper to stronger judges only when needed, while preserving the stated guarantee.
The authors report over 80% agreement at almost 80% coverage on a Chatbot Arena subset using substantially cheaper models.

source_observation.claim: The abstract couples a selective decision rule with an explicit agreement target and reports coverage alongside agreement.

lessons.interpretation: This links the quality objective to the fraction of cases handled automatically, making the operating tradeoff visible.
lessons.application: When presenting an evaluation method, state the target agreement level together with achieved coverage and the escalation policy.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no human reference standard or meaningful selective-decision threshold is available.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, calibration procedure, or statistical construction underlying the claimed guarantees.
Exact baselines, datasets beyond the cited subset, uncertainty ranges, and cost measurements are not reported.
The meaning of “almost 80% test coverage” and the conditions for escalation are unspecified.
